title: CAN_H/CAN_L tightly coupled routing (non-P/N asymmetric names)
rule: CAN_H and CAN_L must be routed as a tightly coupled differential pair on the same layer over a continuous GND reference plane. Because they use asymmetric industry-standard names (not _P/_N), KiCad's auto-diff-pair router does NOT recognize them automatically — they must be routed manually as a coupled pair. Maximum uncoupled stub length: keep stubs to the transceiver (U2 TJA1051T/3) as short as possible, ideally under 5mm.
rationale: Classical CAN at 500kbps is forgiving, but the optional 1Mbps rate (spec §3.1 v3.4) places the bus in the star/stub topology where ringing on uncoupled stubs gates the 1Mbps option. The TJA1051T/3 is NOT a SIC part, so no transceiver-side ringing suppression is available — the passive topology result depends entirely on the PCB coupling and stub geometry. Short coupled stubs to the transceiver are the design defense.

Verify the DRU has no CAN-specific rule (by design — standard diff is adequate per hub-standard.kicad_dru comment). Verify visually/geometrically that CAN_H and CAN_L route in parallel within ~0.2mm gap on the same layer. Check that U2 (TJA1051T/3) is placed close to its RJ-45 port(s).

title: CAN termination 120Ω split at Hub only — never on modules
rule: The fixed 120Ω split termination (two 60Ω resistors + 4.7nF cap) must be present at the Hub and absent on every module. No module may carry CAN termination resistors on the CAN_H/CAN_L bus nets.
rationale: CAN requires exactly one 120Ω termination per stub endpoint on a star topology. The Hub is one endpoint; the other end is terminated by the cable impedance and the spec-defined Hub-only split. A module adding its own termination creates a parallel path that drops the effective termination below 60Ω, causing dominant-bit timing errors and protocol failures. This is a locked platform decision (spec §3.1).
scope: All modules (identify: board is in modules/ directory, not hubs/). On modules: verify no resistors with values 60Ω, 120Ω, or 0.12k are connected between CAN_H and CAN_L. On Hub: verify R3 and R4 (60Ω each) with C7 (4.7nF) form the split termination.
check_method: cec_synth_pipeline CONFORMANCE chk_no_module_can_term: parse netlist for module boards, find any R between CAN_H and CAN_L nets, flag if value is 60Ω or 120Ω. On Hub boards: verify the split termination components exist with correct values.

title: CAN star topology — stub length equalization at Hub
rule: On the Hub, each RJ-45 port's CAN_H/CAN_L stub from the split termination network to the port jack should be kept as equal in length as practical. Maximum stub imbalance advisory: <10mm difference between longest and shortest port stub.
rationale: A star topology with unequal stubs presents different propagation delays per port. At 500kbps this is negligible, but at the optional 1Mbps rate with no SIC transceiver ringing suppression, unequal stubs create asymmetric reflections that can degrade the eye. Equalizing stubs is the cheapest SI improvement available.
scope: Hub boards only (hubs/hub-standard, hubs/hub-pro). Identify CAN_H and CAN_L nets connecting to multiple RJ-45 jacks (J2-J5 on Hub Standard).
check_method: Measure routed length of CAN_H and CAN_L from the R3/R4 split termination to each port jack pad. Compute max-min delta. Flag if delta > 10mm. Requires routed board.

title: FTP shielded RJ-45 SH1/SH2 pads tied to GND
rule: On every board carrying the FTP shielded RJ-45 (cec:RJ45_FTP_Shielded_Horizontal, Kinghelm KH-RJ45-58-8P8C / LCSC C2683360), both shield tab pads SH1 and SH2 must be connected to GND. This applies to: Hub Standard (J2-J5), 12VHPWR Standard (J1), and EPS 8-pin (J1). No unconnected shield tab pads on FTP jacks.

An unconnected shield tab is an EMC failure mode — the cable shield becomes a floating conductor that can re-radiate instead of absorbing. The M3 chassis bond at both Hub and module provides the ground loop path; at intra-case RJ-45 lengths the ground loop impedance is negligible.

Currently applies to: hubs/hub-standard J2-J5, modules/eps-8pin J1, modules/12vhpwr-standard J1. The 24-pin and PCIe boards still use unshielded 54602 — shield constraint does NOT apply to them yet.

title: DETECT pin 8 ESD protection diode on every board
rule: Every Hub port and every module must carry a low-capacitance ESD diode on the DETECT pin 8 line. The correct part is PESD5V0S1BA (SOD-323, LCSC C5261083) — cathode to the DETECT line, anode to GND. PESD5V0S1UL is the wrong package designation (DFN1006/SOD-882 in LCSC stock) — do not use it.
rationale: DETECT feeds the ESP32 ADC directly with no inherent input protection. The platform hot-plugs modules, so insertion ESD lands on a bare analog input. A single low-capacitance ESD diode is a locked platform-wide requirement (spec §2.4 v2.0). Low capacitance (<1pF) is required to not load the 10kΩ/3.3V divider. Locked part: PESD5V0S1BA SOD-323.

Identify the DETECT net by: connected to RJ-45 pin 8, contains 'DETECT' in net name. Identify the ESD diode by: ref D1 (modules) or D2-D5 (hub), SOD-323 footprint, PESD5V0S1BA value. title: DETECT code resistor value matches §2.3 table
rule: The DETECT resistor (R1 on modules, the per-port pull-down on Hub) must match the §2.3 code table for the module's comm-class: CAN-only modules (24-pin, EPS, PCIe, 12VHPWR Standard) = 2.2kΩ (E24, ±1% tolerance acceptable). 12VHPWR Pro = 4.7kΩ. Resistor must be from pin 8 to GND (not pull-up). This is a standard 1% 0402 — no TCR or precision requirement.
rationale: The Hub reads DETECT through a fixed 10kΩ pull-up to 3.3V to determine which link to bring up. A wrong resistor value causes the Hub to misconfigure its port (e.g. attempting RS-485 on a CAN-only module, or vice versa). Codes are spaced ~0.45V apart — a wrong value by even one E24 step may fall in a different code bin.
scope: All modules. Identify: R1 on the DETECT net (net name contains 'DETECT'). Board profile determines expected value: Standard modules = 2.2kΩ; Pro modules = 4.7kΩ. Read from cfg.params['detect_ohms'] in synth pipeline.

Flag if no resistor found or value is wrong. Also verify resistor connects DETECT to GND (not to a power rail).

title: RS-485 streaming pair (pins 4/5) absent on Standard modules and Hubs
rule: Standard-tier modules must NOT populate RS-485 receivers or transmitters on pair 2 (pins 4/5 = STREAM_P/STREAM_N). The STREAM_P/STREAM_N nets on Standard boards must be absent or terminated only with a passive pull-down/stub at the module side. Pro+ boards must populate the RS-485 driver/receiver.
rationale: RS-485 is a tier-differentiating feature (spec §3.2). Populating streaming hardware on a Standard module inflates BOM cost without function (the Standard Hub has no RS-485 receiver). An RS-485 driver on a Standard module would drive the pair unexpectedly if misconfigured, potentially interfering with Pro module streaming on a mixed hub.

title: Continuous GND plane under signal routing (In1.Cu/L2)
rule: CAN_H/CAN_L and USB_D+/D− must route over a continuous solid GND pour on In1.Cu (L2). Anti-pad voids from high-current via arrays in the GND plane must not interrupt the return path directly beneath any of these signal nets. Acceptable: anti-pads displaced laterally from the signal trace with at least one solid GND copper width between the void edge and the trace.
rationale: Return current travels in the GND plane directly beneath differential signal traces. A void in the GND plane under a differential pair forces return current to detour, increasing loop inductance, causing a reference-plane discontinuity, and increasing EMI. High-current via arrays on EPS/PCIe boards punch anti-pad voids in L2 — spec §6.7 explicitly calls out 'keep signal traces and their returns clear of the voids'.
scope: All boards. Identify signal nets requiring continuous GND: /CAN_H, /CAN_L, /USB_D_P, /USB_D_N, /STREAM_P, /STREAM_N. Identify high-current via arrays: clusters of vias on nets containing '12V' or '/SENSEC'. Check that routing of CAN/USB traces on L1 or L4 does not cross over GND plane voids from those via arrays.
check_method: Partial: parse board for ZONE fill polygons on In1.Cu (GND net). Parse via array positions on high-current nets. Verify no differential signal trace segment on any layer passes within its own width of a GND plane anti-pad void. Full check requires geometric intersection analysis of trace bounding boxes vs. zone cutouts.

title: Signal net board-edge clearance — slot-antenna prevention
rule: CAN_H, CAN_L, USB_D_P, USB_D_N, STREAM_P, STREAM_N, and DETECT traces must maintain at least 0.5mm clearance from Edge.Cuts. Traces within 0.2mm of the board edge are at risk of acting as slot antennas, radiating EMI proportional to signal edge rate.
rationale: A trace parallel to and close to a board edge forms a slot antenna at frequencies where the trace length approaches λ/4. CAN at 500kbps–1Mbps has harmonic content up to ~5MHz where even short edge segments can couple. The Hub Standard PCB review (CLAUDE.md action 3c) specifically flagged CAN_RX/CAN_L traces at 0.03–0.13mm from the board edge as a slot-antenna risk.
scope: All boards. Identify affected nets: /CAN_H, /CAN_L, /USB_D_P, /USB_D_N, /STREAM_P, /STREAM_N, /DETECT. Measure minimum distance from any track segment on these nets to the nearest Edge.Cuts line.
check_method: Run kicad-cli pcb drc and check copper_edge_clearance violations on the named nets. Alternatively, parse board for track segments on these nets and compute minimum distance to Edge.Cuts polygons. Flag any segment within 0.5mm. CLAUDE.md cites 0.03–0.13mm as the current Hub Standard failure case.

title: Power netclass trace width ≥ 0.5mm (DRU safety net)

title: Kelvin sense pairs (_HI/_LO) — hard routing gate on connectivity
rule: Every Kelvin sense pair (*_HI and *_LO) must be fully routed with zero unconnected ratlines on both members. This is a HARD GATE: any candidate where either *_HI or *_LO has an unrouted ratline fails outright, regardless of DRC count.
rationale: An unrouted Kelvin tap means the INA sense input is floating — the current measurement is completely wrong or absent. This is a measurement correctness requirement, not a performance optimization. The cec_score.kelvin_ok gate was specifically added to prevent a route from appearing 'mostly done' while the most critical measurement net is disconnected.
scope: All boards with shunts (EPS, PCIe, 24-pin, 12VHPWR). Identify Kelvin pairs by: net name ends in '_HI' and has a counterpart ending in '_LO' with the same stem. E.g. /SENSEC1_HI + /SENSEC1_LO, /IN1_P + /IN1_N (for INA240 filtered inputs). Stems: /SENSEC1, /SENSEC2 on EPS; /SENSEC1-3 on PCIe.
check_method: cec_score._derive_pairs() identifies all *_HI/*_LO pairs. Metrics.kelvin_ok = True iff every pair has >=1 routed track segment AND 0 unconnected ratlines on both members. Run via cec_score.score() -> gate(). Also check cec_synth_pipeline ROUTE_GATE chk_kelvin_gate.

title: Kelvin sense taps on L1 (F.Cu), short, no vias
rule: Kelvin sense taps (*_HI/*_LO from the shunt inner sense pads to the INA input pins) must be routed on L1 (F.Cu) only, must be ≤3mm total length per tap, and must not use any vias. The taps must connect to the shunt's INNER sense terminals (not the force terminals).
rationale: Via inductance and trace length on the Kelvin tap add series impedance that appears in the measurement loop and degrades current accuracy. Spec §6.8 (LOCKED): 'Keep the Kelvin sense pair short and local on the top layer next to the shunt and its monitor. Do not route it down to a signal layer and back, which folds via inductance and trace length into the measurement.' At 0.5mΩ shunt values, even 1Ω trace inductance at AC frequencies matters for transient detection accuracy.
scope: All boards with shunts. Identify Kelvin taps: track segments on *_HI and *_LO nets. Identify shunt placement: RS* components. Check that the tap originates at the shunt inner sense pad (not force pad) and terminates at the INA U* sense input, staying on F.Cu, with no via in between.
check_method: Parse board for tracks on *_HI and *_LO nets. Verify: (1) all track segments are on layer F.Cu (not B.Cu, In1.Cu, In2.Cu); (2) total routed length from shunt pad to INA pad is ≤3mm; (3) no via is present on these nets between the shunt and the INA. NOTE: cec_score.kelvin_ok only checks connectivity — this additional layer/via/length check requires new code. The cec_synth_pipeline MEASURE chk_kelvin_topology checks topology (shunt straddles pair + INA present) but not layer/length.
source: spec §6.8 (LOCKED): 'Keep the Kelvin sense pair short and local on the top layer next to the shunt and its monitor. Do not route it down to a signal layer and back'; CLAUDE.md action -2: 'sense-IC-adjacent-to-shunt as a hard constraint (Kelvin)'; CLAUDE.md stackup: 'L1: sensors and components, including the shunts'

title: INA sense IC must be physically adjacent to its shunt
rule: Each INA238/INA228/INA240/INA181 current-sense IC must be placed immediately adjacent to the shunt it senses (≤3mm between closest IC pad and closest shunt pad). The sense IC must be on the same side of the board as the shunt (both on F.Cu). No other component may be placed between the shunt sense pads and the INA sense input pads.
rationale: The Kelvin sense path length constraint (≤3mm, no vias, L1 only) cannot be satisfied unless the INA is physically adjacent to the shunt. Placement further away forces longer Kelvin traces that violate spec §6.8. CLAUDE.md action item -2 explicitly lists 'sense-IC-adjacent-to-shunt as a hard constraint (Kelvin)' as deferred work that must be added as a hard constraint when the synth placer resumes.
scope: All boards with shunts and INA sense ICs. Identify shunt-to-INA mapping: each cable has one RS* shunt + one U* INA (INA238 for EPS/PCIe, INA228 for 24-pin, INA240 for 12VHPWR, INA181 for §6.13 detection). The INA ref can be derived from netlist: INA inputs IN+ and IN- connect to *_HI and *_LO which connect to the shunt inner pads.
check_method: For each (shunt RS_n, INA U_n) pair identified from netlist: compute Euclidean distance between the INA's closest sense-input pad centroid and the shunt's closest inner sense pad centroid in the placed board. Flag if distance > 3mm or if the INA is on a different board side than the shunt.
source: spec §6.8 (LOCKED); CLAUDE.md action -2: 'adding these as HARD constraints is a LOT more work or an entire reconsideration of the placement approach. WHEN RESUMED, the design pass must add: (2) sense-IC-adjacent-to-shunt as a hard constraint (Kelvin)'

title: INA240 input RC filter: matched 10Ω Rf + 470nF differential cap per channel
rule: On the 12VHPWR Standard module, each INA240 input pair must have matched 10Ω series resistors (RFH_n and RFL_n, 0.1%/50ppm, Yageo RT0402BRE07-10RL or equivalent) on both IN+ and IN− inputs, plus a 470nF differential capacitor (CF_n) across the filtered inputs. fc = 1/(2π × 2×Rf × Cdiff) ≈ 16.9kHz. Both Rf resistors in a pair must use the same value (matched within 0.1%) for CMRR preservation.
rationale: Mismatched Rf resistors degrade the INA240's common-mode rejection ratio (CMRR) at the filter pole. At the ~10kHz GPU transient frequency of interest, even 1Ω mismatch in the 10Ω Rf pair introduces ~40dB CMRR degradation. Spec explicitly: 'matched 10 ohm series Rf on each input (RFH/RFL1-6) + a 470 nF differential cap (CF1-6)' and 'Rf held at 10 ohm + matched (TI's INA240 ceiling) for negligible gain/CMRR error'.
scope: 12VHPWR Standard module only (modules/12vhpwr-standard). Identify: RFH1-6 and RFL1-6 (10Ω 0.1%) + CF1-6 (470nF). Check BOM: both RFH and RFL must be the same MPN (C705642 Yageo RT0402BRE07-10RL or equivalent 0.1% 50ppm 0402).
check_method: Parse BOM for refs RFH1-6 and RFL1-6: verify all 12 have identical value (10Ω), tolerance (0.1%), and MPN. Parse for CF1-6: verify value is 470nF. Check netlist: RFH_n connects between SENSEC_n_HI and IN_n_P; RFL_n connects between SENSEC_n_LO and IN_n_N; CF_n connects between IN_n_P and IN_n_N.
source: CLAUDE.md: 'matched 10 ohm series Rf on each input (RFH/RFL1-6) + a 470 nF differential cap (CF1-6), fc = 1/(2*pi*2*Rf*Cdiff) ~= 16.9 kHz'; spec §6.1 12VHPWR Standard sensing; CLAUDE.md: 'RFH/RFL filter 10ohm DONE 2026-06-06 -> 0.1% Yageo RT0402BRE0710RL (C705642)'

title: VRAIL_DIV ADC input: 1nF C0G cap at R6 junction
rule: The VRAIL_DIV node (output of the 47kΩ/10kΩ rail voltage divider into the ESP32 ADC) must have a 1nF C0G bypass capacitor to GND placed at the divider junction (at R6.1 / VRAIL_DIV node). Value: 1nF C0G (Murata GRM1555C1H102JA01D / LCSC C76947). fc ≈ 19kHz with the 47k||10k Thévenin source impedance.
rationale: The ESP32 SAR ADC requires charge from the S&H network at the ADC input. Without a capacitor at VRAIL_DIV, the ~38kΩ Thévenin source impedance limits charge delivery, causing ADC undersampling error. The 1nF C0G cap serves both the S&H charge reservoir and as an anti-alias filter (fc ≈ 19kHz matches the ~16.9kHz INA RC filter cutoff). C0G dielectric is required — X5R/X7R capacitance changes with bias voltage, adding gain error proportional to the measured rail voltage.
scope: 12VHPWR Standard module only (modules/12vhpwr-standard). Identify: C24 on VRAIL_DIV net. Also applicable to any other board with a 47k/10k divider into an ESP32 ADC (24-pin if it has a divider).
check_method: Parse netlist for VRAIL_DIV net. Verify exactly one capacitor (C24) is present on this net to GND. Verify BOM value = 1nF, dielectric = C0G (from MPN or BOM note). Verify no X5R/X7R capacitor on VRAIL_DIV.
source: CLAUDE.md: 'VRAIL_DIV ADC cap DONE 2026-06-06 -- added C24 = 1nF C0G (Murata GRM1555C1H102JA01D / C76947) VRAIL_DIV->GND, fc~19kHz with the 47k||10k source'; spec §6.1 12VHPWR Standard

title: REF3030 ratiometric reference bypass caps present
rule: The REF3030 (U4 on 12VHPWR Standard) must have both input and output bypass capacitors per the datasheet (typically 100nF on IN and 100nF on OUT, C0G or X7R, placed within 2mm of U4 pins). The REF3030 OUT must connect only to ESP32 ADC1 IO8 — not to any other load.
rationale: A voltage reference without bypass capacitors is susceptible to oscillation and noise coupling from adjacent switching regulators. The REF3030 is measured by the ADC for ratiometric correction — noise on its output directly adds measurement error. The spec explicitly adds bypass caps to the REF3030 BOM (CLAUDE.md v3.8 note: 'REF3030 (3.0V, SOT-23, cec-vendor:REF3030, MPN REF3030AIDBZR) + 2 bypass caps').
scope: 12VHPWR Standard module only. Identify: U4 with value REF3030 or REF3030AIDBZR. Check adjacent bypass caps on IN (pin 1) and OUT (pin 2) nets.
check_method: Parse netlist for U4 (REF3030). Verify at least one capacitor connects between U4 pin 1 (IN, net +3V3) and GND, and at least one capacitor connects between U4 pin 2 (OUT, net VREF) and GND. Verify VREF net connects to ESP32 ADC1 IO8 and no other load component (other than the ADC input and the bypass cap).
source: CLAUDE.md v3.8: 'REF3030 (3.0V, SOT-23, cec-vendor:REF3030, MPN REF3030AIDBZR) + 2 bypass caps'; spec §6.1: 'REF3030 OUT to ADC1 IO8 (freed by moving the SENSE0 sideband tap to IO15)'

title: TJA1051T/3 CAN transceiver bypass caps on VCC and VIO
rule: The TJA1051T/3 (U2 on all boards) must have: a 100nF bypass cap on VCC (pin 3, +3V3 or +5V per variant), a 100nF bypass cap on VIO (pin 5, +3V3), placed within 2mm of the respective pins. VCC and VIO must not share a single bypass cap.
rationale: The TJA1051T/3 datasheet requires separate decoupling on VCC and VIO. Without individual bypass caps, CAN transceiver switching transients couple onto the +3V3 rail and into adjacent signal lines. The CLAUDE.md 'decoupling brought up to the 24-pin gold standard' note specifically calls out 'dedicated TJA1051T/3 VCC/VIO bypass' as a requirement.
scope: All boards with TJA1051T/3 (U2 on all boards). Identify by: component value = 'TJA1051T/3' or 'TJA1051'. Check for bypass caps C_U2_VCC and C_U2_VIO (or by net: caps on +3V3 adjacent to U2).
check_method: Parse netlist for U2 (TJA1051). Find capacitors within 2mm of U2 (by BOM proximity or by net: caps on the +3V3 and VIO nets that also connect to U2 supply pins). Verify at least two caps are present (one per supply pin). Verify each is 100nF (value in BOM). Flag if missing or if VCC and VIO share one cap.
source: CLAUDE.md: 'dedicated TJA1051T/3 VCC/VIO bypass — the module U2 value is now TJA1051T/3 (C38695)'; spec §3.1 TJA1051T/3 locked; TJA1051T/3 datasheet decoupling requirement

title: M3 mounting holes GND-tied for chassis ground bond
rule: All M3 mounting holes (MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via footprint) must be connected to the GND net via their copper pad. No M3 mounting hole may be isolated (no-connect or unconnected pad). The GND copper from the mounting pad must form a direct low-impedance path to the In1.Cu GND pour.
rationale: M3 screws into an aluminum chassis provide the low-impedance chassis ground bond that closes the EMC shield loop. An isolated mounting hole leaves the board floating relative to chassis, eliminating chassis-bond filtering and degrading radiated emissions. Spec §4: '4x M3 corner holes, chassis-grounded (MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via)'.
scope: All boards. Identify mounting holes: refs H1-H4 (or MK*) with footprint MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via. Verify each is on GND net.
check_method: Parse netlist for all mounting hole components (footprint contains 'MountingHole' and '3.2mm'). For each, verify pad 1 net is GND. Any mounting hole with an unconnected pad or explicit no-connect on its pad is a violation.
source: CLAUDE.md: '4x M3 corner holes, chassis-grounded (PC-standard fastener; MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via)'; spec §4 Hub Standard table; spec §6.6 thermal design: 'Couple the high-current copper to the chassis through the mounting points'

title: SK6812 LED data line 3.3V→5V level shift buffer required
rule: The SK6812 LED data input line (DL1.DIN on Hub Standard) must be driven through the SN74AHCT1G08 (U6, configured as buffer with both inputs tied to LED_DATA GPIO) + 330Ω series resistor (R14) + 100nF bypass cap (C14 on U6 VCC). The ESP32 GPIO must NOT drive the LED data line directly at 3.3V.
rationale: The SK6812 V_IH threshold at 5V VDD is 0.7 × VDD = 3.5V. The ESP32 GPIO drives only 3.3V — below the guaranteed V_IH. Direct drive causes unreliable LED initialization and intermittent wrong color/behavior, especially on power-up. The AHCT buffer input uses TTL threshold (~2V), so 3.3V ESP GPIO reliably drives it, and the AHCT output is 5V-rail logic, reliably high for the SK6812. The 330Ω series resistor limits inrush to the first LED input capacitance.
scope: Hub Standard board only (the only board with SK6812 LEDs). Identify: DL1 (SK6812 chain, 7 LEDs). Check U6 = SN74AHCT1G08 (or equivalent AHCT AND gate configured as buffer). R14 = 330Ω between U6 output and DL1.DIN. C14 = 100nF on U6 VCC pin.
check_method: Parse netlist: verify U6 (value = SN74AHCT1G08 or 74AHCT1G08) exists with both input pins connected to the LED_DATA net. Verify U6 output connects to R14, and R14 output connects to DL1 (SK6812 first LED) DIN. Verify C14 (100nF) on U6 VCC between VCC and GND. Verify ESP32 GPIO (IO25) connects to U6 inputs, NOT directly to DL1.DIN.
source: CLAUDE.md: 'SK6812 data level shift (2026-06-05): the ESP32's 3.3 V GPIO is below the 5 V SK6812 V_IH (0.7*VDD ~= 3.5 V), so the LED data line is buffered up to 5 V by U6 (SN74AHCT1G08 single 2-input AND with both inputs tied = a non-inverting AHCT buffer; SOT-23-5, VCC=+5VSB, C14 100 nF) with R14 330 ohm series into DL1.DIN'; spec §4 Hub Standard table

title: NanoKVM aux UART lines: 33Ω series resistors + ESD clamp on KVM_3V3_REF
rule: On the Hub Standard J7 NanoKVM aux header: UART TX (J7 pin 3) and UART RX (J7 pin 4) must each have a 33Ω series resistor (R19 and R20) between the header pin and the ESP32 GPIO. The KVM_3V3_REF line (J7 pin 5) must have a PESD5V0S1BA ESD clamp (D7, cathode to KVM_3V3_REF, anode to GND).
rationale: The NanoKVM UART lines exit the board on a cable — any external cable is an antenna. The 33Ω series resistors damp reflections and limit inrush current if the NanoKVM's UART pin is driven before the Hub boots (collision protection). The PESD5V0S1BA on KVM_3V3_REF protects the ESP32 ADC1 IO1 pin from ESD on the cabled reference line (same rationale as the DETECT pin ESD diode — CLAUDE.md: 'D7 (PESD5V0S1BA, C5261083) ESD-clamps the cabled ref pin').
scope: Hub Standard only (hubs/hub-standard, J7 = S5B-PH-K-S 5-pin right-angle JST-PH). Identify: R19 (33Ω on J7.TX→ESP IO11), R20 (33Ω on J7.RX→ESP IO12), D7 (PESD5V0S1BA on J7.KVM_3V3_REF→GND).
check_method: Parse netlist: verify R19 and R20 (value ≈ 33Ω) on the UART_TX and UART_RX nets between J7 pins 3/4 and ESP32 IO11/IO12. Verify D7 (value = PESD5V0S1BA, footprint SOD-323) with cathode on KVM_3V3_REF net and anode on GND. Flag if any element is missing.
source: CLAUDE.md action item 0: 'UART TX -> 33ohm R19 -> ESP IO11, 4 = UART RX -> 33ohm R20 -> ESP IO12'; 'D7 (PESD5V0S1BA, C5261083) ESD-clamps the cabled ref pin'; spec §2.9 NanoKVM aux header

title: §6.13 detection comparator threshold RC: 10kΩ + 100nF PWM filter
rule: On EPS/PCIe Standard modules, the firmware-settable comparator threshold path must include: MCU PWM output (THRESH_PWM / IO14) → 10kΩ series resistor (R10) → 100nF shunt cap (C40) to GND → TLV7011 REF+ input. The RC filter fc = 1/(2π × 10kΩ × 100nF) ≈ 159Hz, smoothing the PWM to a stable DC threshold voltage.
rationale: Without the RC filter, the PWM signal drives the comparator reference directly, causing the comparator to toggle at the PWM frequency (typically tens of kHz) rather than triggering on actual load transients. This would produce thousands of false FREEZE triggers per second. The 159Hz filter cutoff is slow enough to present a stable DC reference while still allowing firmware to change the threshold setting in ~10ms.
scope: EPS 8-pin and PCIe 8-pin modules after §6.13 implementation (modules/eps-8pin, modules/pcie-8pin-2port, modules/pcie-8pin-3port). Identify: R10 (10kΩ) on THRESH_PWM net, C40 (100nF) between THRESH node and GND, feeding TLV7011 REF+ input.
check_method: Parse netlist: find R10 with one end on THRESH_PWM net and one end on THRESH node. Find C40 between THRESH node and GND. Find TLV7011 (U30-32) REF+ input connected to THRESH node. Verify value R10 = 10kΩ, C40 = 100nF. Flag if RC network is absent or if THRESH_PWM connects directly to comparator REF+ without filter.
source: CLAUDE.md: '§6.13 chain netlist-verified per cable (shunt SENSE_HI -> INA181A2 gain-50 -> TLV7011 comparator -> firmware THRESH (MCU PWM IO14 + R10 10k/C40 100n) -> per-cable DET -> MCU GPIO latch, ORs into FREEZE)'; spec §6.13

title: High-current via arrays must not block signal routing corridors
rule: On EPS and PCIe boards, the via arrays beneath each cable shunt (vertical transition for ~40-55A) must be contained within the cable column (the region directly under the J_IN/J_OUT connector pair and shunt). No via must be placed in the signal routing corridor (the central band between cable columns used for I2C, CAN, THRESH, DETECT spine routing).
rationale: CLAUDE.md action -2 explicitly requires 'high-current corridor keepout + pour reservation' as a deferred hard constraint for the synth placer. High-current vias in the signal spine force the router to detour CAN_H/CAN_L, I2C, and THRESH traces around via anti-pad voids, increasing trace length and potentially breaking the GND plane continuity check. The spec §6.7 'keep signal traces and their returns clear of the voids' is the normative basis.
scope: EPS 8-pin and PCIe 8-pin modules. Identify cable columns: x-regions from J_IN to J_OUT pads. Identify signal corridor: x-region between the outermost cable column edges, toward the control/logic side of the board. Identify high-current vias: vias on nets containing '12V' or '/SENSEC' or on GND net within the cable column region.
check_method: Parse board for via positions on high-current nets. Compute the cable column bounding boxes (from J_IN/J_OUT pad centroids ±half the connector width). Verify all high-current vias are within cable column bounding boxes. Flag any high-current via in the signal corridor region between columns.
source: spec §6.7: 'Via arrays punch anti-pad voids in the L2 ground pour; keep signal traces and their returns clear of the voids'; CLAUDE.md action -2: 'high-current corridor keepout + pour reservation' as deferred hard constraint; cec_fr.add_power_pours() implementation

title: Hub Pro USB High Speed 90Ω ±5% differential impedance (advisory pending Pro spec)
rule: When Hub Pro is fully specified, USB_D_P/USB_D_N must be routed to 90Ω ±5% differential impedance for USB High Speed (480Mbps). Track width and gap must be calculated from the actual Hub Pro PCB stackup using a field solver or the JLCPCB impedance calculator. Skew between D+ and D− must be ≤5ps (inter-pair delay matching).
rationale: USB High Speed at 480Mbps requires 90Ω ±5% differential impedance (USB 2.0 specification). The Hub Standard uses Full Speed (12Mbps) where ±15% is tolerable — the hub-standard.kicad_dru comment explicitly notes 'FS is impedance-tolerant, so on THIS (Standard) board ~90ohm diff is good-practice-not-critical -- the strict 90ohm discipline matters on Hub Pro (USB High Speed, 480 Mbps)'. This constraint should be promoted to hard when Hub Pro PCB is laid out.
scope: Hub Pro only (hubs/hub-pro). Currently soft/advisory because Hub Pro is not yet fully specified. When Hub Pro PCB exists: apply impedance-controlled layer stackup, calculate W/S for 90Ω differential, set USB netclass in .kicad_pro to those dimensions, order impedance-controlled from JLCPCB.
check_method: When Hub Pro PCB exists: verify .kicad_pro USB netclass diff_pair_width and diff_pair_gap match the stackup-calculated 90Ω values (from JLCPCB impedance calculator for the specific prepreg/core stackup). Verify no USB HS track deviates >±5% from target width. Currently not checkable (board not yet laid out).
source: hubs/hub-standard/hub-standard.kicad_dru lines 36-47: 'the strict 90ohm discipline matters on Hub Pro (USB High Speed, 480 Mbps)'; spec §5 Hub Pro: 'USB High Speed'

title: RJ-45 8P8C is the ONLY permitted module-to-Hub link connector
rule: Every board's module-to-Hub interface must use an RJ-45 8P8C connector. No Molex Mini-Fit Jr, JST, or any other connector family is permitted on the link or on Hub bulk-power lines. Exception: the 24-pin ATX module J3/J4 PSU-side power path and the 12VHPWR board-mount 12V-2x6 are explicitly not link connectors and are exempt.
scope: All boards: every connector whose nets include VCC/GND/CAN_H/CAN_L/DETECT/STREAM must be RJ-45. Check by net membership of the link set.
rationale: Mini-Fit Jr retired platform-wide as the module-to-Hub interconnect (spec §2.1). The RJ-45 was locked at the platform level for the commodity-cable, any-cable-length property.
check_method: For every non-RJ45 connector footprint, verify that NONE of its nets are in the set {VCC, +5VSB, GND, CAN_H, CAN1_H, CAN_L, CAN1_L, DETECT, STREAM_P, STREAM_N}.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §2.1: 'Module-to-Hub connector is RJ-45 (8P8C) for all tiers, all modules and Hubs. Mini-Fit Jr is retired platform-wide.'

title: RJ-45 link connector must use the FTP shielded footprint (Kinghelm KH-RJ45-58-8P8C)
rule: Every RJ-45 link connector must use the footprint cec:RJ45_FTP_Shielded_Horizontal (Kinghelm KH-RJ45-58-8P8C, LCSC C2683360). Unshielded Amphenol 54602 (C2847314) is acceptable only on prototype boards; any board entering production must carry the FTP footprint.
scope: All RJ-45 link connectors on Hub Standard (J2-J5), Hub Pro, EPS 8-pin (J1), 12VHPWR Standard (J1), and any regenerated 24-pin/PCIe boards.
rationale: Spec §2.1 LOCKS FTP jacks platform-wide. The authoritative MPN is the Kinghelm KH-RJ45-58-8P8C (C2683360). CLAUDE.md: 'FTP migration (2026-06-06): Hub, 12VHPWR Standard AND EPS now carry the platform FTP jack.'
check_method: Check BOM MPN or LCSC field on every RJ-45 link connector — must match C2683360 or footprint name must contain 'RJ45_FTP_Shielded_Horizontal'. Flag if still on C2847314/54602.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §2.1: 'Shielded jacks (FTP) on Hub and modules.' CLAUDE.md locked decisions: 'MPN LOCKED (single shielded 8P8C, metal shell, right-angle TH, 1.5A).'

title: RJ-45 FTP jack shield tabs SH1 and SH2 must both be tied to GND net
rule: On every RJ-45 FTP connector (cec:RJ45_FTP_Shielded_Horizontal), the two metal-shell ground tabs (pads SH1 and SH2) must be connected to the GND net. No-connect on either shield tab is a violation.
scope: All FTP RJ-45 connectors on all boards (Hub Standard J2-J5, EPS J1, 12VHPWR-Std J1, any board carrying the FTP footprint).
rationale: CLAUDE.md: 'Shield SH1/SH2 TIED TO GND (both ends shielded AND grounded, per user — Hub+module share the PC chassis on a short RJ-45 so both-end grounding wins at HF).'
check_method: From the netlist, for every RJ-45 connector with pads named SH1 and SH2, verify each pad's net name resolves to GND or the board GND net. A no-connect or open net on SH1/SH2 fails.
source: CLAUDE.md FTP migration note (2026-06-06): 'SH1/SH2 -> GND (both-end shielding+grounding, per the user).'

title: RJ-45 pin 1 must carry VCC (+5VSB) net
rule: RJ-45 pad 1 on every module-to-Hub link connector must be connected to a net named VCC or +5VSB. Exception: the 24-pin ATX module's RJ-45 pin 1 (J1 pin 1) must be NO-CONNECT (not tied to the module's +5VSB supply).
scope: All module RJ-45 link connectors. Special-cased for the 24-pin ATX module J1 where pin 1 is no-connect by design.
rationale: Spec §2.2 pin allocation table: pin 1 = VCC (+5VSB). Spec §2.7: '24-pin module dual-feed (LOCKED, v3.3): its RJ-45 VCC pin (J1 pin 1) is left no-connect — not tied to the module's +5VSB.'
check_method: net_of(rj45_ref, '1') must contain 'VCC' or '5VSB'. For the 24-pin ATX module specifically, net_of(J1, '1') must be empty/no-connect.
existing_checker: chk_pin_allocation (cec_synth_pipeline.py, pin '1' check) NOTE (merged dup): chk_pin_allocation is partial -- it does not yet enforce the 24-pin pin-1 NO-CONNECT exception.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §2.2 pin allocation table; §2.7 dual-feed lock.

title: RJ-45 pin 2 must carry GND net
rule: RJ-45 pad 2 on every module-to-Hub link connector must be connected to GND.
scope: All module RJ-45 link connectors on all boards.
rationale: Spec §2.2 pin allocation table: pin 2 = GND (power return). Paired with pin 1 on the same twisted pair for low-impedance power delivery.
check_method: net_of(rj45_ref, '2') must contain 'GND'.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §2.2: 'Pin 2 — GND (power return) — All.'

title: RJ-45 pin 3 must carry CAN_H net
rule: RJ-45 pad 3 on every module-to-Hub link connector must be connected to the CAN1_H (or CAN_H) net.
scope: All module and Hub RJ-45 link connectors.
rationale: Spec §2.2: pin 3 = CAN1_H, pair 3, used on all tiers for classical CAN control traffic.
check_method: net_of(rj45_ref, '3') must match /CAN.*H/i.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §2.2: 'Pin 3 — CAN1_H (control plus low-rate telemetry) — All.'

title: RJ-45 pin 6 must carry CAN_L net
rule: RJ-45 pad 6 on every module-to-Hub link connector must be connected to the CAN1_L (or CAN_L) net.
scope: All module and Hub RJ-45 link connectors.
rationale: Spec §2.2: pin 6 = CAN1_L, pair 3 (the T568B split pair, stays twisted in the cable). Classical CAN differential pair.
check_method: net_of(rj45_ref, '6') must match /CAN.*L/i.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §2.2: 'Pin 6 — CAN1_L — All.'

title: RJ-45 pin 7 must be a reserved spare — NOT AUX_REF or any driven signal
rule: RJ-45 pad 7 must be connected to a reserved/spare net or left no-connect. Any net named AUX_REF, REF, or carrying a driven signal is a violation.
scope: All module and Hub RJ-45 link connectors.
rationale: Spec §2.2: pin 7 = Reserved spare (no distributed reference). Spec §3.3 resolved OQ-3: NO distributed reference; pin 7 is a reserved spare. CLAUDE.md: 'pin 7=reserved-not-AUX_REF' in CONFORMANCE checklist.
check_method: net_of(rj45_ref, '7') must NOT match /AUX|REF/i. If the net is named anything other than a reserved/spare/NC equivalent, flag it.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §2.2: 'Pin 7 — Reserved spare (no distributed reference; see Section 3.3).' §3.3: 'Pin 7 is a reserved spare.'

title: RJ-45 pin 8 must carry DETECT net connected to the code resistor divider
rule: RJ-45 pad 8 must be connected to the DETECT net. That net must include a code resistor (R-prefixed component) from DETECT to GND matching the §2.3 table: 2.2 kΩ for CAN-only Standard modules, 4.7 kΩ for CAN+RS-485 (12VHPWR Pro).
scope: All module RJ-45 link connectors. Hub side: pad 8 connects to Hub ADC input through a 10 kΩ pull-up to 3.3V.
rationale: Spec §2.3 DETECT resistor encodes link capability read by the Hub ADC. OQ-6 resolved v1.7. The 3.3V pull-up (NOT 5VSB) keeps the divider output inside ESP32 ADC range.
check_method: net_of(rj45_ref, '8') matches /DETECT/i. The DETECT net has at least one R-prefixed component. That component's value is within 10% of 2200 Ω (Standard CAN-only) or 4700 Ω (Pro RS-485) per the board profile.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §2.3 DETECT code table. CLAUDE.md: 'DETECT code table RESOLVED v1.7 (OQ-6)'.

title: RJ-45 pins 4 and 5 (RS-485 STREAM pair) must be unpopulated/terminated on Standard modules
rule: On Standard-tier modules, RJ-45 pads 4 and 5 must not connect to any RS-485 transceiver (THVD, MAX348x, SN65HVD, SP3485, or similar). Pins 4/5 are terminated at the module side but carry no active driver. Pro+ modules may populate the streaming pair.
scope: Standard modules: 24-pin ATX, EPS 8-pin, PCIe 2-port, PCIe 3-port, 12VHPWR Standard.
rationale: Spec §2.2: pins 4/5 = STREAM_P/STREAM_N, Pro+ only. Spec §3.2: 'Present on Pro modules and Pro+ Hubs. Standard does not populate it.'
check_method: chk_rs485_tiering: for Standard-profile boards, verify no RS-485 transceiver part is present in the BOM or netlist. Also verify pins 4/5 net names do not resolve to active driven nets.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §2.2; §3.2: 'RS-485 carries high-bandwidth telemetry streaming exclusively... Present on Pro modules and Pro+ Hubs. Standard does not populate it.'

title: RJ-45 connector mouth must face the board edge (not inboard)
rule: Every RJ-45 link connector must be placed at the board edge with its mating mouth (cable-entry side) facing outward toward the nearest board edge. The connector body may overhang the edge; pads must remain on-board. Rotation=90 places the mouth toward the right edge on Hub Standard; on module boards the mouth faces the right edge.
scope: All boards carrying RJ-45 link connectors.
rationale: CLAUDE.md layout guide: 'J1 (RJ-45) and J5 (USB-C) overhang the RIGHT edge.' gen-module-pcb.py places RJ-45 at rot=90 on the right edge. Functional requirement: the cable must mate without the PCB blocking plug insertion.
check_method: Render the board and verify no RJ-45 connector is placed interior (more than ~5 mm from any edge). The pad row must be <= board_edge + overhang; the connector body may extend past edge.
source: CLAUDE.md gen-module-pcb.py description: 'USB-C (J5) and RJ-45 (J1) are rotated 90 so they mate OUTWARD on the right edge.' LAYOUT-GUIDE.md: 'Place-first items: 4x RJ-45 along back edge.'

title: Hub bulk power input must be a dedicated 2-pin JST-XH connector (S2B-XH-A), separate from the RJ-45 interface
rule: Every Hub board must carry a dedicated 2-pin JST-XH power-in connector (working selection: S2B-XH-A) for the +5VSB bulk feed from the 24-pin ATX module. This connector is SEPARATE from all RJ-45 ports. The 24-pin module feeds this connector; the Hub distributes 5VSB to each port over the RJ-45 VCC pin.
scope: Hub Standard (J_5VSB / J1), Hub Pro (analogous), all future Hubs.
rationale: Spec §2.7 OQ-1 LOCKED: 'The Hub receives bulk power on a dedicated 2-pin power-in connector, separate from the RJ-45 interface... Working selection: 2-pin JST-XH (~3A class).'
check_method: The Hub netlist must contain a 2-pin connector with both pins on +5VSB and GND nets, whose footprint is JST_XH_S2B-XH-A (or similar 2-pin XH-class). This connector must be distinct from any RJ-45 connector.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §2.7: 'The connector architecture is locked; the specific part is the simplest one meeting the rating... Working selection: 2-pin JST-XH (~3A class).'

title: NanoKVM aux header must be a 5-pin RIGHT-ANGLE JST-PH (S5B-PH-K-S, C157923) — not top-entry B5B
rule: The Hub NanoKVM auxiliary header (J7 on Hub Standard) must use the S5B-PH-K-S right-angle JST-PH 5-pin connector (LCSC C157923, footprint JST_PH_S5B-PH-K-S_1x05_P2.00mm_Horizontal). The top-entry B5B-PH-K-S (C157993) is explicitly prohibited — the right-angle form locks v3.9/v3.10 so the cable exits parallel to the board edge.
scope: Hub Standard J7 (NanoKVM aux header). Applies to all future Hub boards.
rationale: Spec §2.9 and §4 NanoKVM aux link row: 'S5B-PH-K-S (LCSC C157923; footprint ... Horizontal)' RIGHT-ANGLE LOCKED v3.7/v3.10. CLAUDE.md: 'changed from top-entry B5B-PH-K-S/C157993 per the v3.9 right-angle correction so the NanoKVM cable exits a board edge.'
check_method: Hub netlist: find the 5-pin JST-PH connector. Its BOM LCSC field must be C157923 (S5B-PH-K-S), NOT C157993 (B5B-PH-K-S). Footprint must contain 'Horizontal' (not 'Vertical').
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §4 Hub Standard table: 'Reserved keyed 5-pin right-angle JST-PH header (S5B-PH-K-S, C157923; form LOCKED v3.7, right-angle v3.10).' CLAUDE.md v3.9 note.

title: NanoKVM aux header pin assignment: 1=+5VSB, 2=GND, 3=UART_TX, 4=UART_RX, 5=KVM_3V3_REF
rule: The 5-pin JST-PH NanoKVM aux header must carry: pin 1 = +5VSB (shared subsystem rail), pin 2 = GND, pin 3 = UART TX (to ESP32 via 33Ω series R), pin 4 = UART RX (from ESP32 via 33Ω series R), pin 5 = NanoKVM 3.3V reference/presence. No trigger GPIO is present on this header.
scope: Hub Standard J7 and all future Hub NanoKVM aux headers.
rationale: Spec §2.9 and CLAUDE.md: 'Pins: 1 = +5VSB (shared §2.9 rail), 2 = GND, 3 = UART TX -> 33ohm R19 -> ESP IO11, 4 = UART RX -> 33ohm R20 -> ESP IO12, 5 = NanoKVM 3V3 ref. NO trigger GPIO.'
check_method: From the Hub netlist, for the 5-pin NanoKVM connector: net_of(J7,'1') contains '5VSB'; net_of(J7,'2') = GND; net_of(J7,'3') goes through a 33Ω resistor to ESP IO11; net_of(J7,'4') goes through a 33Ω resistor to ESP IO12; net_of(J7,'5') is a 3V3_REF sense net.
source: CLAUDE.md §2.9 action item 0(a): 'Pins: 1 = +5VSB (shared §2.9 rail), 2 = GND, 3 = UART TX -> 33ohm R19 -> ESP IO11, 4 = UART RX -> 33ohm R20 -> ESP IO12, 5 = NanoKVM 3V3 ref.'

title: 24-pin ATX module PSU-side connectors J3 and J4 must both be Molex Mini-Fit Jr 5569 24-circuit MALE headers
rule: The 24-pin ATX module must carry two Molex Mini-Fit Jr (5569 family) 24-circuit MALE right-angle headers: J3 on the PSU side (input) and J4 on the motherboard side (output). Both connectors must be male (pin-side, not socket). The footprint is cec-Connector_Molex:Molex_Mini-Fit_Jr_5569-24A1_2x12_P4.20mm_Horizontal or equivalent.
scope: 24-pin ATX module only (modules/atx-24pin).
rationale: Spec §2.8: 'two Molex Mini-Fit Jr (5569 family) 24-circuit male headers: one on the PSU side (J3) and one on the motherboard side (J4)... both connectors are male.' No board-mount female 24-pin ATX receptacle exists as a standard part.
check_method: 24-pin netlist: verify J3 and J4 are both 24-circuit Mini-Fit Jr (footprint contains '5569' or '24A1' or '24-circuit'). Verify both are MALE headers (not receptacle). Verify no female-receptacle variant is used.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §2.8: 'The module carries two Molex Mini-Fit Jr (5569 family) 24-circuit male headers: one on the PSU side (input, J3) and one on the motherboard side (output, J4).'

title: EPS module PSU-side connectors must be Molex 87427-0802 2x04 RA with correct GND/+12V pinout
rule: The EPS 8-pin module interposer connectors (J_IN1, J_OUT1, J_IN2, J_OUT2) must use the Molex 87427-0802 right-angle 2x4 header (footprint cec-Connector_Molex:Molex_Mini-Fit_Jr_87427-0802_2x04_P4.20mm_RA). Pin assignment: pads 1-4 = GND, pads 5-8 = +12V (SENSE*_HI/LO nets). The FLIPPED assignment (1-4=+12V, 5-8=GND) is a violation.
scope: EPS 8-pin module (modules/eps-8pin), J_IN1, J_OUT1, J_IN2, J_OUT2.
rationale: CLAUDE.md: 'Corrected to GND on pads 1-4, +12V on pads 5-8 in the schematic (netlist-verified all 4: pins1-4=GND, pins5-8=SENSE*_HI on J_IN / SENSE*_LO on J_OUT).' EATX12V/EPS12V standard pinout.
check_method: For each EPS interposer connector: net_of(Jx, '1'..'4') must match GND net; net_of(Jx, '5'..'8') must match SENSE*_HI or SENSE*_LO net. Footprint must be the 87427-0802 (no snap pegs, mirrored: pads in -x, 2nd row -y).
source: CLAUDE.md EPS power-connector pinout fix (2026-06-06): 'GND on pads 1-4, +12V on pads 5-8.' CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §2.8 EPS interposer.

title: PCIe module PSU-side connectors must be Molex 45586-0005 2x04 with 4.20mm/5.50mm pitch
rule: The PCIe 8-pin module interposer connectors (J_IN, J_OUT per cable) must use the Molex 45586-0005 2x04 right-angle header (footprint cec-Connector_Molex:Molex_Mini-Fit_Jr_45586_2x04_P4.20mm_Horizontal). Real geometry: 4.20mm pin pitch, 5.50mm row spacing (NOT 4.20mm — the square-grid error). Round pads 2.3622mm diameter / 1.8542mm drill; two 3.048mm snap pegs.
scope: PCIe 2-port (modules/pcie-8pin-2port) and PCIe 3-port (modules/pcie-8pin-3port), all J_IN/J_OUT connectors.
rationale: CLAUDE.md: 'LOCKED 2026-06-06: Molex 45586-0005... Real land: 4.20mm pitch + 5.50mm ROWS.' The 4.20mm row-spacing error was explicitly corrected.
check_method: Verify footprint on each PCIe interposer connector matches the 45586-0005 land (4.20mm pitch, 5.50mm row). Check no square-grid footprint (4.20mm x 4.20mm) is used.
source: CLAUDE.md PCIe cable connector LOCKED (2026-06-06): 'Molex 45586-0005... Real land: 4.20mm pitch + 5.50mm ROWS, round 2.3622mm pads / 1.8542mm drill.'

title: EPS/PCIe interposer J_IN must be at the top edge (rot=180), J_OUT at the bottom edge (rot=0)
rule: On EPS and PCIe interposer modules, the PSU-side input connector (J_IN) must be placed at the TOP board edge with rotation 180° (mouth facing up/out), and the load-side output connector (J_OUT) must be at the BOTTOM board edge with rotation 0° (mouth facing down/out). J_IN and J_OUT for cable N must be in the same vertical column so the high-current path is straight top-to-bottom.
scope: EPS 8-pin module, PCIe 2-port module, PCIe 3-port module. All J_IN/J_OUT pairs.
rationale: CLAUDE.md gen-module-pcb.py description: 'N cables inline (PSU-side IN on the top edge, load-side OUT on the bottom — 12V flows top->bottom through each cable's 2-pad R_2512 shunt + INA238).' The 87427-0802 footprint is mirrored so J_IN rot=180, J_OUT rot=0 produces aligned columns.
check_method: For each cable N on EPS/PCIe: J_IN_N.y < board_center.y (top half), J_OUT_N.y > board_center.y (bottom half). J_IN_N.rotation ≈ 180°; J_OUT_N.rotation ≈ 0°. Both connectors within ~2mm of same x-column.
source: CLAUDE.md gen-module-pcb.py: 'J_IN rot180 / J_OUT rot0 (87427 is mirrored).' gen-module-pcb.py JIN_Y=10.0, placement() function.

title: EPS/PCIe interposer connector bodies may overhang board edge; pads must remain on-board
rule: The Molex 87427-0802 (EPS) and 45586-0005 (PCIe) connector bodies and mating mouths may extend PAST the board edge (overhang), but all solder pads must be on-board (within the Edge.Cuts boundary). The board edge should pass through the connector courtyard, not past the pads.
scope: EPS 8-pin module J_IN/J_OUT, PCIe 2-port/3-port J_IN/J_OUT.
rationale: CLAUDE.md: 'The PLUG connectors OVERHANG their edge so a cable seats without the board fouling the plug overmold while the solder pads stay on-board.' Area saving: 'cable column ~22->~14mm' with overhang.
check_method: For each J_IN/J_OUT: all pad centers must be inside Edge.Cuts polygon. Courtyard may cross the edge. DRC copper-to-edge must be 0 (pads inside) but courtyard-to-edge crossing is acceptable.
source: CLAUDE.md EPS 8-pin PCB re-condensed (2026-06-06): 'pegless connector keeps only its pad rows on-board and overhangs the whole body/mouth.' gen-module-pcb.py: 'connectors OVERHANG their edge.'

title: 12VHPWR module connectors must use CEC_12V2x6_Horizontal (Molex 219116 / 2191161161)
rule: The 12VHPWR Standard and Pro modules must use footprint cec:CEC_12V2x6_Horizontal for both J3 (input) and J4 (output) connectors. MPN: Molex 2191161161 (T&R) or 2191160161 (tray). Real geometry: 3.0mm pin pitch / 3.0mm row pitch, power drill 1.067mm / pad 1.52mm, signal drill 0.61mm / pad 1.14mm. NO other 12VHPWR footprint is acceptable.
scope: 12VHPWR Standard module (modules/12vhpwr-standard) J3 and J4. 12VHPWR Pro module when built out.
rationale: CLAUDE.md: 'Footprint cec:CEC_12V2x6_Horizontal is now the OFFICIAL Molex footprint (LOCKED 2026-06-05): Molex 219116 / PCIe CEM5 12V-2x6 right-angle THT header, MPN 2191161161.'
check_method: Check footprint field on J3 and J4: must be 'cec:CEC_12V2x6_Horizontal' or equivalent. Check MPN BOM field contains '219116' or '2191161161'.
source: CLAUDE.md 12VHPWR connector lock (2026-06-05): 'CEC_12V2x6_Horizontal is now the OFFICIAL Molex footprint (LOCKED 2026-06-05): Molex 219116.'

title: 12VHPWR J3 must be at the top edge (rot=180, mouth up), J4 at the bottom edge (rot=0, mouth down)
rule: On the 12VHPWR module, J3 (PSU-side input) must be placed at the TOP edge with rotation=180° so the connector mouth faces upward/outward. J4 (GPU-side output) must be at the BOTTOM edge with rotation=0° so the mouth faces downward/outward. NOTE: the generator's older placement used rot=0/180 (reversed) — use the spec-corrected rotations.
scope: 12VHPWR Standard module J3 (input) and J4 (output). 12VHPWR Pro when built.
rationale: CLAUDE.md: 'the generator's placement_hpwr J3/J4 ROTATIONS are now stale for this footprint (its mouth is on +y, so mouth-out-the-edge needs J3 rot 180 / J4 rot 0, not 0/180).' J3 at top with rot=180 means current flows top-to-bottom through the 6 per-pin lanes.
check_method: J3.rotation ≈ 180°, J3.y < board_height/2 (top half). J4.rotation ≈ 0°, J4.y > board_height/2 (bottom half).
source: CLAUDE.md 12VHPWR connector lock: 'its mouth is on +y, so mouth-out-the-edge needs J3 rot 180 / J4 rot 0, not 0/180.'

title: 12VHPWR connector pads 1-6 must be +12V, pads 7-12 must be GND — verify against CEM5.1
rule: On the CEC_12V2x6_Horizontal footprint: pads 1-6 must connect to the +12V rail/nets, pads 7-12 must connect to GND, pads 13-16 are sideband (SENSE0, SENSE1, CARD_CBL_PRES#, CARD_PWR_STABLE). A swap of +12V and GND rows shorts +12V to GND. This assignment must be verified against PCIe CEM5.1 before powering any board.
scope: 12VHPWR Standard module J3 and J4. 12VHPWR Pro module when built.
rationale: CLAUDE.md SAFETY note: 'VERIFY pins 7-12 = GND (i.e. 1-6 = +12V) against PCIe CEM5.1 / the target GPU before powering, since the schematic ties 7-12 to the GND plane (a swap shorts +12V to GND).'
check_method: From netlist: net_of(J3, '1'..'6') must contain '+12V' or 'SENSE*_HI'. net_of(J3, '7'..'12') must contain 'GND'. net_of(J3, '13'..'16') must be SENSE0/SENSE1/CARD_CBL_PRES/CARD_PWR_STABLE nets.
source: CLAUDE.md locked decisions §2.8: 'pins 1-6 = +12V (the row ADJACENT to the signal pins), 7-12 = GND (the OUTER row), 13-16 = sideband S1..S4.'

title: 12VHPWR connectors are soldered to the board — no detachable pass-through header or bridging cable on the module
rule: The 12VHPWR module's 12V-2x6 connectors are board-mounted THT right-angle headers soldered directly to the PCB. No detachable intermediate connector or bridging cable is permitted in the inline power path. The GPU-side output (J4) connects via a captive soldered pigtail.
scope: 12VHPWR Standard and Pro modules.
rationale: Spec §2.8: 'The 12VHPWR module does not use detachable pass-through headers and does not need a bridging cable. Its 12VHPWR (12V-2x6) connector(s) are soldered directly to the module PCB.' Removing an extra mated pair from the melt-prone connector reduces failure risk.
check_method: BOM inspection: no removable/plug-in 12V-2x6 receptacle connector present. J3 and J4 must be board-mount THT connectors (MPN 2191161161), not cable-crimp connectors.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §2.8: 'Its 12VHPWR (12V-2x6) connector(s) are soldered directly to the module PCB.'

title: M3 mounting holes must be chassis-grounded (MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via, pad on GND net)
rule: All M3 mounting holes must use the MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via footprint (3.2mm drill, pad with via). Each mounting hole pad must be connected to the GND net (chassis ground bond). NPTH (no-connect) mounting holes are a violation.
scope: All boards: Hub Standard (4x M3 at corners), all modules (3x M3).
rationale: Spec §4 Hub Standard table: '4x M3 corner holes, chassis-grounded (PC-standard fastener; MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via).' CLAUDE.md: '4 M3 chassis-grounded mounting.' The chassis bond provides ESD and EMC path.
check_method: All M-prefixed mounting hole references: footprint must be MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via (not NPTH). Pad net must be GND. Drill must be 3.2mm.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §4: '4x M3 corner holes, chassis-grounded (PC-standard fastener; MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via).'

title: Hub Standard must have 4x M3 mounting holes at the four board corners
rule: The Hub Standard PCB must carry exactly four M3 mounting holes (MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via, GND-connected) placed near the four corners of the board. Spacing from edge: minimum ~2mm. Each hole must be clear of connector courtyards and any component keepouts.
scope: Hub Standard board (hubs/hub-standard).
rationale: Spec §4: '4x M3 corner holes, chassis-grounded.' Hub Standard actual board has M1 at (76,96.25), M2 at (162,96.25), M3 at (76,158), M4 at (162,158) — verified from PCB file.
check_method: Count M-prefixed mounting holes on Hub Standard board: must be exactly 4. Check each is near a corner quadrant. No courtyard overlap with connectors.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §4 Hub Standard table. Hub-standard PCB: M1-M4 at the four board corners.

title: Sensing modules must carry 3x M3 mounting holes (2 on logic/right side, 1 on connector/left side)
rule: Each sensing module PCB must carry exactly three M3 mounting holes (MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via, GND-connected): two near the logic/right side corners (TR and BR), and one centered on the connector/left side at the board's midheight. The three-mount pattern ensures the high-current connector side is mechanically anchored.
scope: EPS 8-pin module, PCIe 2-port module, PCIe 3-port module, 12VHPWR Standard module.
rationale: CLAUDE.md gen-pcie-condensed.py: 'TWO on the logic/right side (TR/BR corners) + ONE centered on the connector/left side at (4,H/2).' gen-module-pcb.py: '3 M3 mounts (2 left strip, 1 bottom-right below the RJ-45).'
check_method: Count M-prefixed mounting holes: must be exactly 3. Two holes within the right-side third of the board; one hole within the left-side third at mid-height. All GND-connected.
source: CLAUDE.md gen-pcie-condensed.py description (2026-06-06): 'TWO on the logic/right side (TR/BR corners) + ONE centered on the connector/left side at (4,H/2) — matches the 2-port arrangement.'

title: M3 mounting holes must not overlap any connector courtyard
rule: No M3 mounting hole courtyard or pad may overlap with any connector's courtyard (RJ-45, USB-C, power connectors, JST headers). Minimum clearance: 1mm from any connector courtyard edge.
scope: All boards, all M3 mounting holes.
rationale: CLAUDE.md: 'four corner M3 mounts (MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via) stay clear of the connectors.' Physical requirement: the mounting screw must not contact or deform a connector.
check_method: DRC courtyard check: run kicad-cli drc and verify no courtyard_overlap between mounting holes and connectors. Alternatively check geometric distance between hole center and nearest connector courtyard edge > 1mm.
source: CLAUDE.md gen-module-pcb.py: 'the four corner M3 mounts (MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via) stay clear of the connectors.'

title: CAN transceiver must be TJA1051T/3 — TJA1462A and any CAN-FD transceiver are forbidden
rule: Every board's CAN transceiver must be the TJA1051T/3 (LCSC C38695, classical high-speed CAN, VIO=3.3V, SOIC-8). The TJA1462A and any other CAN-FD or SIC transceiver are explicitly prohibited platform-wide.
scope: All boards with a CAN transceiver: Hub Standard (U2), all generated modules (U2). 12VHPWR Pro and Hub Pro inherit when built out.
rationale: Spec §3.1 v3.5: 'LOCKED to the classical part (spec §3.1 v3.5, 2026-06-05): with FD deferred platform-wide the FD/SIC-capable TJA1462A no longer earns its place.' CLAUDE.md: 'STATUS (2026-06-05, DONE): propagated to every board.'
check_method: For each U-prefixed CAN transceiver: BOM value must be 'TJA1051T/3', LCSC must be C38695. Any BOM entry with 'TJA1462' or 'FD' in the value is a violation.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §3.1: 'Transceiver: TJA1051T/3... LOCKED to the classical part v3.5.' CLAUDE.md: 'TJA1051T/3 (C38695).'

title: USB-C connector must be at the board edge (mouth outward) adjacent to the MCU
rule: The USB-C flash/debug connector (J5 on modules) must be placed at the right board edge (or top edge) with its mouth facing outward. It must be positioned adjacent to the ESP32 MCU to minimize USB D+/D- trace length. Maximum trace length from ESP32 USB pads to USB-C connector: 20mm.
scope: All module boards with USB-C (J5): EPS, PCIe, 12VHPWR Standard, 24-pin ATX.
rationale: CLAUDE.md: 'USB-C (J5) and RJ-45 (J1) are rotated 90 so they mate OUTWARD on the right edge.' USB D+/D- differential pair (kelvin_ok equivalent) must be short to minimize stub effects.
check_method: J5 (USB-C) must be within 5mm of the board right or top edge. Center of J5 must be within 25mm of ESP32 U1 center. Trace from ESP USB_D_P/USB_D_N pins to J5 must be < 20mm (verify with HPWL or actual route length).
source: CLAUDE.md gen-module-pcb.py: 'USB-C (J5) and RJ-45 (J1) are rotated 90 so they mate OUTWARD on the right edge.' EPS netlist USB diff-pair: '/USB_D_P, /USB_D_N'.

title: USB D+/D- must be routed as a matched differential pair
rule: The USB full-speed differential pair (net names /USB_D_P and /USB_D_N, or /USB_DP and /USB_DM) must be routed as a matched differential pair: equal length (length match within 0.5mm), parallel routing, 0.25mm trace width, 0.13mm gap, no vias if avoidable.
scope: All module boards: EPS (U1 pins 18/17 to J5 A6/B6, A7/B7), PCIe, 12VHPWR Standard, 24-pin ATX.
rationale: cec_score diffpair_ok HARD GATE: both _P and _N members must be routed with 0 unconnected ratlines. EPS netlist renamed /USB_DP->/USB_D_P, /USB_DM->/USB_D_N for KiCad diff-pair auto-recognition. Spec §3.1: USB HS is the Hub host link, requiring a clean diff pair.
check_method: cec_score.diffpair_ok gate: for (/USB_D_P, /USB_D_N) pair, both members routed, 0 unconnected ratlines. DRU USB class: 0.25mm trace, 0.13mm gap enforced by kicad_dru.
source: CLAUDE.md EPS netclasses: 'USB 0.25 diff gap0.13 /USB_D_P,/USB_D_N.' cec_score.py _RE_DIFF_P = re.compile(r'^(.+)_P$').

title: All library paths must be ${KIPRJMOD}-relative — no absolute or machine-global paths
rule: Every entry in sym-lib-table and fp-lib-table must use ${KIPRJMOD}-relative paths. No absolute paths (C:/, /home/, etc.) and no bare stock KiCad library nicknames (Package_SO, Connector_JST, etc.) without the cec- prefix.
scope: All boards: sym-lib-table, fp-lib-table, all .kicad_sch footprint references, all .kicad_pcb footprint refs.
rationale: CLAUDE.md KiCad environment: 'Library paths are project-relative via ${KIPRJMOD}.' and 'Library-table NICKNAMES must be namespaced cec / cec-*... A bare stock nickname collides with the same-named machine-global KiCad library... this bit us once.'
check_method: Parse sym-lib-table and fp-lib-table: all 'uri' fields must start with '${KIPRJMOD}'. All library nicknames must start with 'cec'. Flag any path starting with a drive letter, '/', or '~'.

title: Each board must carry at least 3 fiducial marks for pick-and-place assembly
rule: Every board intended for JLCPCB assembly must carry at least 3 fiducial marks (footprint cec-Fiducial:Fiducial_1mm_Mask2mm or equivalent), placed at non-collinear positions forming a triangle. At least 2 fiducials should be near opposite corners. Fiducials must be marked board_only, excluded from BOM and position files.
scope: All boards with JLCPCB assembly intent: Hub Standard, EPS 8-pin, PCIe 2/3-port, 12VHPWR Standard.
rationale: CLAUDE.md: 'fiducials DONE 2026-06-06 (3x cec-Fiducial:Fiducial_1mm_Mask2mm, board_only/excl-BOM/excl-pos, refs on F.Fab: FID1 (162.25,61) TR, FID2 (166,135.5) BR, FID3 (139,116) lower-center).' JLCPCB assembly requirement for SMT pick-and-place.
check_method: Count FID-prefixed references on each board. Must be >= 3. Check they form a non-collinear triangle (area > 0). Check board_only=true (no position in CPL, no BOM row).
source: CLAUDE.md 12VHPWR BOM sourcing note: 'fiducials DONE 2026-06-06 (3x cec-Fiducial:Fiducial_1mm_Mask2mm).'

title: Hub Standard must carry exactly 4 RJ-45 link ports (J2-J5)
rule: The Hub Standard PCB must carry exactly four RJ-45 8P8C shielded connectors (J2, J3, J4, J5) forming the four module ports. Each must use the FTP footprint. They should be co-located along one edge (the 'back' or module-facing edge) in a row.
scope: Hub Standard board (hubs/hub-standard). Hub Pro will have 8.
rationale: Spec §4: 'Topology: Star, 4 ports. Connector: 4x RJ-45 8P8C, locking boot.'
check_method: Count RJ-45 connectors on Hub Standard: must be exactly 4. All must carry the FTP footprint cec:RJ45_FTP_Shielded_Horizontal.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §4 Hub Standard table: 'Topology: Star, 4 ports. Connector: 4x RJ-45 8P8C, locking boot.'

title: Hub +5V_HOLD hold-up capacitor must be Panasonic EEVFK1C472M 4700µF / 16V aluminum electrolytic
rule: The Hub Standard +5V_HOLD hold-up capacitor (C1) must be a 4700µF / 16V aluminum electrolytic capacitor (Panasonic EEVFK1C472M or equivalent). Polymer capacitor at this value is unobtainable and is explicitly prohibited. Connected behind the reverse-isolation Schottky D1, on the isolated +5V_HOLD node.
scope: Hub Standard C1 (+5V_HOLD hold-up). Hub Pro analogous.
rationale: Spec §4 Hub Standard table: 'Hold-up: 4700 uF / 16 V aluminum electrolytic on the isolated +5V_HOLD node (Panasonic EEVFK1C472M); corrected from aluminum polymer (unobtainable at 4700 uF).'
check_method: BOM: C1 value must be 4700µF, voltage >= 16V. BOM type must be aluminum electrolytic (not polymer). MPN should match EEVFK1C472M or equivalent series.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §4: '4700 uF / 16 V aluminum electrolytic on the isolated +5V_HOLD node (Panasonic EEVFK1C472M).'

title: All shunts must be four-terminal Kelvin type — 2-pad R_2512 footprint is the schematic placeholder
rule: Every shunt resistor on all modules must be a four-terminal Kelvin-sense type (force terminals carry current; sense taps are separate). The schematic uses a 2-pad R_2512 footprint (per CLAUDE.md: 'honest 2-pad R_2512 (Kelvin taps drawn in copper at layout, §6.8) — NOT the 4-terminal WSK2512'). The Kelvin sense tap geometry is a layout task.
scope: All shunt resistors on all modules: RS1/RS2 on EPS, RS1-RS3 on PCIe 3-port, RS1-RS6 on 12VHPWR Standard, RS1-RS4 on 24-pin ATX.
rationale: Spec §6.4: 'low-TCR metal-element / metal-strip precision shunt, tight tolerance, four-terminal Kelvin, power rating well above the dissipation.' spec §6.8: 'Four-wire Kelvin sensing on every shunt.'
check_method: All RS-prefixed components must have footprint R_2512 (or 2512-variant). BOM must specify a four-terminal Kelvin shunt (WSK2512, CSS2H-2512, or equivalent). Value must match §6.4 table: 0.5mΩ for EPS/PCIe, 1mΩ for 12VHPWR, 2mΩ/25mΩ for 24-pin.
existing_checker: chk_shunt_values (cec_synth_pipeline.py CONFORMANCE stage, checks value tolerance)
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.4. CLAUDE.md: 'Shunt land = honest 2-pad R_2512 (Kelvin taps drawn in copper at layout, §6.8).'

title: RJ-45 link connector must have a documented current rating of at least 1.5A per contact
rule: The selected RJ-45 8P8C connector MPN must have a manufacturer-specified contact current rating of at least 1.5A. The Kinghelm KH-RJ45-58-8P8C (C2683360) meets this as 1.5A. The Wuerth 615008137421 (C132217) was declined due to non-matching land pattern. The Amphenol 54602 (C2847314, unshielded) is also 1.5A-rated — acceptable for prototype only.
scope: All RJ-45 link connectors on all boards.
rationale: CLAUDE.md locked decisions: 'Connector must have a documented current rating of at least 1.5A.' Spec §2.5: 'many connectors are rated 1.5A or higher.'
check_method: BOM MPN lookup: verify the datasheet of the selected RJ-45 connector lists a per-contact current rating >= 1.5A. Flag if no MPN or if MPN datasheet shows < 1.5A.
source: CLAUDE.md locked decisions: 'Connector must have a documented current rating of at least 1.5A.' Spec §2.5.

title: EPS/PCIe high-current shunt sites should have a TIM pad and bare contact land for chassis thermal coupling
rule: The EPS and PCIe module PCBs must specify a bare (un-anodized) contact land on the back copper facing the chassis, under the high-current shunt sites, with a thermal interface material (TIM) pad. This provides a thermal path to the anodized 6063 aluminum chassis to control shunt self-heating and preserve low-TCR accuracy.
scope: EPS 8-pin module shunt RS1/RS2. PCIe 2-port RS1/RS2. PCIe 3-port RS1/RS2/RS3.
rationale: Spec §6.6 design-review decision v3.8: 'Spec a TIM pad and a bare, un-anodized contact land under the high-current EPS/PCIe shunts, where the 0.8 to 1.5 W of dissipation makes the self-heating term dominant.' The corner M3 screws are only point contact.
check_method: Check for copper pours or exposed copper regions on B.Cu under the shunt footprint area. Check documentation for TIM pad callout. This is a layout and assembly note; not fully auto-checkable from netlist alone.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.6: 'Spec a TIM pad and a bare, un-anodized contact land under the high-current EPS/PCIe shunts.'

title: CAN H/L must be on RJ-45 pins 3 and 6 (T568B pair 3) — the split pair that stays twisted in the cable
rule: CAN_H must be on pin 3 (T568B white-green) and CAN_L on pin 6 (T568B green). These are pair 3 — the T568B split pair — and they stay twisted in any Cat5e cable, providing the intended differential CAN protection. Do not reassign CAN to any other pin pair.
scope: All RJ-45 link connectors on all boards.
rationale: Spec §2.2 note: 'Pair 3 (pins 3 and 6) is the T568B split pair but stays twisted in the cable; standard practice for differential CAN.' This is both a pin-allocation constraint and a physical cable constraint.
check_method: Same as chk_pin_allocation pins 3 and 6 checks. Verify CAN_H on pin 3 AND CAN_L on pin 6 simultaneously — they must be on the split pair, not reassigned to adjacent pins.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §2.2: 'Pair 3 (pins 3 and 6) is the T568B split pair but stays twisted in the cable; standard practice for differential CAN.'

title: Each decoupling cap must be placed at its owner IC power pad
rule: Every bypass/decoupling capacitor must be placed within the courtyard envelope of its owner IC (or immediately adjacent, outside but touching the courtyard edge), on the same side of the board. The net shared between cap and IC must match verify_passives() expectations.
scope: All C* refs where the net is a power rail (+3V3, +5VSB, VBUS, VCC) and the cap is <=1 uF. Ownership derived by derive_passive_spec() / auto_cluster() from strongest net coupling to an IC power pin.
rationale: Decoupling caps must be close to their IC's power pins to suppress switching noise; a cap parked far away has high inductance and provides no benefit. cec_pcb.auto_cluster() places each cap just outside the owner IC courtyard edge nearest the power pad.
check_method: For each (cap, owner IC) pair from derive_passive_spec: compute Euclidean distance between cap centroid and nearest power pad of owner IC. Fail if distance > (IC_courtyard_half_diagonal + cap_courtyard_half_diagonal + 1.5 mm clearance).
source: CLAUDE.md done-items: 'PASSIVE ENGINE = every decoupling/RC/pull-up/ESD passive placed in its OWNER IC cluster from a netlist-verified ownership spec (PASSIVE_SPEC: part->IC->expected net), re-checked at build by verify_passives() (25/25 verified)'

title: Sense IC (INA238/INA240/INA181) must be adjacent to its shunt inner edge
rule: Each INA238, INA240, or INA181 sense IC must be placed such that its IN+ and IN- pads (the Kelvin sense inputs) are within 3 mm of the inner sense-tap edge of its associated shunt resistor. No other components may be interposed between the shunt inner edge and the INA sense pins.
scope: All U* refs with footprint containing INA238, INA240, or INA181. For each, find the shunt RS* that shares the *_HI/*_LO nets. Inner shunt edge = pad 1 for _HI net (upper at rot270), pad 2 for _LO net (lower at rot270).
rationale: Kelvin four-wire sensing requires the voltage taps to originate at the shunt inner pad edges, not the outer force-current pads. A long trace from shunt to INA picks up IR drop from supply/return current. CLAUDE.md action item -2 explicitly calls this out as a hard constraint that the auto-placer must enforce.
check_method: For each (INA_ref, shunt_ref) pair sharing *_HI/*_LO nets: compute distance between INA IN+/IN- pad global positions and shunt inner-edge pad global positions. Fail if > 3 mm.
existing_checker: cec_score.kelvin_ok (gates on routed connectivity, not placement distance)
source: CLAUDE.md action item -2: '(2) sense-IC-adjacent-to-shunt as a hard constraint (Kelvin)'; cec_pcb.py auto_cluster docstring; gen-eps-condensed.py: INA238 at (Xc+0.5, 17.5) with shunt at (Xc+6.8, 17.5)

title: Kelvin sense traces must route on F.Cu only, no layer changes
rule: The *_HI and *_LO Kelvin sense net traces from shunt inner pads to INA sense inputs must be routed entirely on F.Cu (the top copper layer), with zero vias between shunt pad and INA input pin. They must run over the In1 GND plane for controlled impedance return.
scope: All nets matching *_HI or *_LO suffixes (Kelvin pairs as derived by cec_score._derive_pairs). Trace segment layer must be F.Cu for all segments from shunt pad to INA pin.
rationale: A via in a Kelvin sense path adds contact resistance and inductance. The sense path must be a low-resistance, low-inductance direct copper path. Routing over the GND plane (In1) gives a short, well-defined return.
check_method: For each Kelvin net, inspect all routed track segments. If any segment is not on F.Cu, or if any via exists on the net between shunt pad and INA pad, fail.
source: CLAUDE.md done-items routing plan: 'Kelvin pairs Cmts.User... sense off the INNER shunt edges, RC filter at the INA'; gen-eps-condensed.py: 'Kelvin taps confirmed non-crossing'; 12VHPWR routing plan: 'Kelvin pair 0.2-0.25mm tight matched pair over the In1 GND plane, sense off the INNER shunt edges'

title: Kelvin taps must originate from inner shunt pad edges, not outer
rule: The *_HI Kelvin tap must connect to pad 1 of its shunt (the pad facing the sense IC / inner edge at rot270), and *_LO must connect to pad 2 (the lower inner edge). The trace must leave from the inner-facing edge of the pad, not the outer force-current edge.
scope: All RS* shunt footprints with rot270 orientation on EPS/PCIe boards. Pad 1 = _HI (upper/inner), pad 2 = _LO (lower/inner).
rationale: The entire point of Kelvin (four-wire) sensing is to pick up the voltage across the shunt body at the exact points where current enters and exits, not including the via/pad contact resistance. Tapping the outer pad edge measures contact resistance in addition to the shunt.
check_method: Inspect shunt rotation: must be rot270 on EPS/PCIe. Confirm pad 1 net is *_HI and pad 2 net is *_LO in the netlist. Verify no net assignment inversion.
source: gen-eps-condensed.py: 'P[f"RS{c}"] = (Xc + 6.8, 17.5, 270)' and 'Kelvin route data: taps from inner shunt edge at (rsx, 15.9) and (rsx, 19.1)'; CLAUDE.md done-items: 'shunt rot 90->270 so HI is the upper terminal'

title: Kelvin _HI and _LO traces must be length-matched within 0.5 mm
rule: For each Kelvin pair (*_HI / *_LO), the total routed copper length from shunt pad to INA sense pin must be matched within 0.5 mm between the two members of the pair.
scope: All (*_HI, *_LO) net pairs as derived by cec_score._derive_pairs. Measure track length on F.Cu only.
rationale: A length mismatch in the Kelvin pair creates a net-resistance asymmetry between IN+ and IN- paths, introducing a small differential offset voltage. For the near-DC current sense application this is a second-order error, but it should be minimized to keep the Kelvin geometry clean.
check_method: Sum F.Cu track lengths for each member of a Kelvin pair. Compute |L_HI - L_LO|. Fail if > 0.5 mm.
existing_checker: cec_score (HPWL / track length metrics available, not yet per-pair length)
source: CLAUDE.md done-items 12VHPWR: 'length-match the straight run in the GUI if the inner/outer spread matters'; spec §6.8 Kelvin sensing

title: INA240 RC anti-alias filter (RFH/RFL + CF) must be placed at INA input pins
rule: For each INA240 on the 12VHPWR Standard board, the matched 10-ohm series filter resistors (RFH_n, RFL_n) and 470 nF differential cap (CF_n) must be placed within 2 mm of the INA240 IN+/IN- pads. RFH and RFL must be equidistant from the INA to maintain CMRR.
scope: 12VHPWR Standard board only. Parts: RFH1-6 / RFL1-6 (10 ohm, 0.1%) and CF1-6 (470 nF). Owner ICs: INA240 instances U_pin1 through U_pin6 (or equivalent refs).
rationale: The RC filter sets fc ~16.9 kHz (-3 dB) to pass 10 kHz GPU transients at -1.3 dB while attenuating HF. The TI application note caps Rf at 10 ohm to limit gain/CMRR degradation. If RFH/RFL are not matched in position relative to the INA, there is a CMRR imbalance. Placement at the INA pins keeps the filtered sense path short.
check_method: For each INA240 instance, find its RFH_n and RFL_n resistors. Measure distance from RFH_n/RFL_n to INA IN+ and IN- pads respectively. Fail if > 2 mm. Verify RFH_n and RFL_n are equidistant from their respective INA pads within 0.3 mm.
source: CLAUDE.md spec v3.4 additions: '(a) a per-channel INA240 input anti-alias/transient RC filter — matched 10 ohm series Rf on each input (RFH/RFL1-6) + a 470 nF differential cap (CF1-6), fc = 1/(2*pi*2*Rf*Cdiff) ~= 16.9 kHz... Rf held at 10 ohm + matched (TI's INA240 ceiling)'

title: Six INA240 must be in 6 symmetric columns at equal pitch
rule: The six INA240 per-pin sense ICs on the 12VHPWR Standard board must be arranged in 6 columns of equal spacing (nominal 6 mm pitch). Each column must be vertically aligned with its shunt resistor and the corresponding J3/J4 connector pin pair. Column pitch must be uniform: max deviation between adjacent column X-positions <= 0.1 mm.
scope: 12VHPWR Standard board. INA240 refs and their paired shunts (RS1-RS6) plus J3/J4 power pin columns.
rationale: Each 12V pin of the 12V-2x6 connector carries independent current. The fan-out layout assigns one column per pin, enabling equal-length Kelvin taps and equal-length high-current traces from J3 through shunt to J4. Asymmetric columns would create length-mismatched sense paths and unequal thermal loading.
check_method: Extract X-positions of INA240 instances. Sort. Compute differences between adjacent X values. Fail if max(differences) - min(differences) > 0.2 mm (non-uniform pitch).
source: gen-hpwr-route-status.py: 'LANE_X = [116.875+6*k for k in range(6)]'; CLAUDE.md: 'six +12V lanes splay symmetrically to a ~6mm SENSE pitch so each lane gets its OWN column'

title: 12VHPWR J3 (in) must be at top edge, J4 (out) at bottom edge, shunts between
rule: On the 12VHPWR Standard board: J3 (PSU input) must be placed at the top board edge (min Y, mouth facing up/out), J4 (GPU output) at the bottom edge (max Y, mouth facing down/out). All shunt resistors RS1-RS6 must have Y-coordinates strictly between J3 connector pad Y-positions and J4 connector pad Y-positions.
scope: 12VHPWR Standard board. J3, J4, RS1-RS6.
rationale: 12V current flows top-to-bottom: PSU cable enters J3 at top, flows down through each shunt (measurement point), and exits J4 to GPU. This straight vertical current path minimizes inductance, ensures each shunt is in the single current path, and allows the two outer copper layers to carry 12V vertically in parallel for low resistance.
check_method: Verify J3 Y-centroid < J4 Y-centroid. Verify all RS* Y-centroids satisfy J3_Y < RS_Y < J4_Y.
source: gen-hpwr-route-status.py: 'J3 at y=62.67, J4 at y=131.83'; CLAUDE.md: '12V power path TOP->BOTTOM down the centre-left (J3 MALE header IN top-centre... J4 captive-pigtail OUT bottom-centre)'

title: Control ICs and decoupling caps must not be placed in the 12V high-current corridor
rule: The 6-column 12V high-current corridor (bounding box from leftmost J3 +12V pin column to rightmost, extended top-to-bottom between J3 and J4) must be free of all non-power-path components: no ESP32, CAN transceiver, LDO, or signal-path passives inside this corridor.
scope: 12VHPWR Standard board. Corridor: X from left-column J3 pin minus 1 mm to right-column J3 pin plus 1 mm, Y from J3 pad top to J4 pad bottom. Exclude: RS1-RS6, INA240 instances, RFH/RFL, CF caps.
rationale: The high-current corridor carries up to ~40A aggregate (6 pins x ~6.7A each). Logic components inside the corridor would (a) be subjected to magnetic field from the current loops, (b) interfere with copper pour routing, (c) create thermal coupling from high-I2R heating. Action item -2 explicitly calls out corridor keepout as a hard constraint.
check_method: Define corridor_bbox from J3/J4 pin positions. For each non-power-path component, check if its courtyard_bbox overlaps corridor_bbox. Fail on any overlap.
source: CLAUDE.md action item -2: '(1) high-current corridor keepout + pour reservation'; gen-hpwr-route-status.py: corridor implicitly defined by LANE_X array

title: REF3030 must be adjacent to ESP32 ADC pin, VREF trace < 10 mm
rule: U4 (REF3030, 3.0V reference) on the 12VHPWR Standard board must be placed within 5 mm of the ESP32-S3-MINI-1 ADC1 IO8 pin pad. The VREF net trace from REF3030 OUT to ESP32 IO8 must be <= 10 mm total length.
scope: 12VHPWR Standard board only. U4 = REF3030, U1 = ESP32-S3-MINI-1, net VREF.
rationale: REF3030 is the ratiometric reference measured by the ESP32 ADC (firmware divides all INA240 outputs by the REF3030 reading to cancel ADC gain/offset drift). The VREF trace must be short and routed away from noisy 12V traces to avoid injecting noise into the reference measurement. REF3030 OUT = 3.0V, must remain within ESP32 ADC input range (< 3.3V absolute max).
check_method: Compute distance between U4 centroid and U1 IO8 pad global position. Fail if > 5 mm. If tracks are routed, sum VREF track length; fail if > 10 mm.
source: gen-hpwr-route-status.py: 'REF3030 U4+bypass planned at (149.8, 98.0) near ESP'; CLAUDE.md v3.8: 'REF3030 (3.0V, SOT-23, measured on ESP ADC1 IO8 for ratiometric correction)'

title: 12VHPWR Standard must use REF3030 (3.0V), not REF3033 (3.3V)
